1.1: 1.1 Prologue. The Book of Wisdom is nowhere found among the Hebrews. Hence its very style smacks more of Greek eloquence. The Jews affirm that it is by Philo. It is called Wisdom because in it the coming of Christ, who is the wisdom of the Father, and his passion are plainly expressed. Love justice, etc. RAB. on the book of Wisdom, vol. 3. Jerome asserts that this book is not by Solomon, etc., up to Love justice, etc. Earth. That is, you prudently restrain the flesh, lest it become proud against the spirit. As if to say: Seek first the kingdom of God Matth. 6., etc. In simplicity. That is, subject yourselves to his will and keep his commandments; as if he said: You who do not understand, do not find fault, because the secrets of God cannot be grasped by human reason, since his judgments are incomprehensible and his ways unsearchable Rom. 11..
1.4: 1.4 For into a malicious, etc. That is, into the animal man, according to the saying: The animal man perceives not I Cor. 2., etc. And therefore he did not say spirit, that is, a spiritual soul. RAB. The philosophers, and heretics, and false Christians flatter themselves in vain. For only the pure of heart can receive the wisdom of God.
1.6: 1.6 Benevolent. He inveighs against those who say that good and evil thoughts are sent in by God, whereas God wills all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. For he tempts no one in order to deceive, but in order to prove; hence: God tempted Abraham Gen. 22.; and, Prove me and tempt me Psal. 25., etc. But each one is tempted by his own concupiscence, and by the just judgment of God is permitted to fall, since he would not obey the spirit of truth.
1.7: 1.7 And that which contains all things. That is, the Spirit, who governs and rules all things. Or, he who reaches from end to end has knowledge of the voice, that is, he grants men understanding of the Scriptures. Or, that which contains all things, that is, man, who has a fitting agreement with every creature. He has knowledge of the voice, that is, of different tongues, by the Holy Spirit, who gave the apostles to speak the great works of God in different tongues. Or that which contains all things, that is, the Holy Spirit, who fills all things by his essence; he has knowledge of the voice, that is, of the Word of God, that is, he is of the same knowledge as the Word. Or, this which contains all things, that is, the Church, in which to one is given the word of knowledge, etc. RAB. He who in the beginning was borne over the waters, and by his majesty fills and contains every creature.
1.8: 1.8 Therefore. RAB. As the elect receive the gift of knowledge and piety through the Spirit, so the reprobate, puffed up by their pride, shamelessly proclaim their error; since they cannot hide from the Spirit of God, nor escape just punishment: for as the eyes of the Lord are upon the just, and his ears unto their prayers, so the face of the Lord is upon them that do evil.
1.11: 1.11 Keep yourselves, therefore. RAB. Murmurings and detractions are ruinous; hence: For detractors and whisperers are hateful to God Rom. 1.; hence: He that detracts from any thing, bindeth himself for the time to come Prov. 13.. The mouth that lieth. THE SAME. A lie is of lighter guilt, etc., up to and the good itself he rewards.
1.12: 1.12 Seek not. THE SAME. He enumerated the things that are harmful to man, etc., up to but rather from vice.
1.16: 1.16 And pacts. We have struck a covenant with death, and with hell we have made a pact.
2.1: 2.1 For they said. RAB. The voice of the lost, etc., up to and we shall be brought to nothing.
2.2: 2.2 Because smoke. Truly we shall be nothing, because smoke and breath are in our nostrils, that is, in our body; that is, our body is compared to smoke and breath, which arise and fail together. And speech a spark. That is, the soul is comparable to a spark, which at once becomes nothing; speech, I say, that is, the soul. To move our heart. That is, it gives life to the body. And that it is to be so expounded, he proves by adding: Because when it is extinguished, the body shall be ashes, and afterwards, the spirit shall be poured abroad
2.10: 2.10 Let us oppress. RAB. These words pertain generally to those, etc., up to nor do they obey even the head, but blaspheme and accuse.
2.17: 2.17 Let us see. RAB. Similar things are said in the Gospel, where the chief priests and Pharisees took counsel how to deliver Jesus to death; and when he was placed on the cross they mocked him, saying: He saved others, himself he cannot save, etc. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross Matth. 27., etc.
2.20: 2.20 By a most shameful death. That is, by the cross, which until the passion of Christ was the punishment of criminals, and is now the trophy of victory.
2.23: 2.23 For God. That is, God is not the author of evils; for he created man for immortality, who, consenting to the devil's suggestion, was made subject to the sentence of death.
3.1: 3.1 But the souls of the just. RAB. In the previous chapter the opinion of the wicked was set out, etc., up to hence: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints Psal. 115..
3.7: 3.7 Sparks. A spark does two things, namely it quickly changes the reed-bed, and it takes vengeance.
3.8: 3.8 And the Lord shall reign. With whom the members also shall reign. Hence in Daniel: The kingdom and power, and the greatness of the kingdom, which is under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High Dan. 7..
3.11: 3.11 Wisdom. RAB. Heretics can be noted in this sentence, etc., up to but shows that the work of the reprobate is worthy of eternal curse.
3.13: 3.13 For blessed. THE SAME. In the barren woman and the eunuch the order of virgins can be understood, etc., up to in the will of the mind, not in weakness of the body.
3.18: 3.18 In the day of acknowledgment. That is, of judgment, when the elect, acknowledged by their judge, will be invited to possess the kingdom; but the wicked will be given no consolation of hope of restoration, but, to be tormented for ever, will be driven from the sight of the supreme King.
4.1: 4.1 O how beautiful is, etc. RAB. Having rebuked the heretics and schismatics, he praises the Catholics, etc., up to and therefore he says: With glory, etc.
4.2: 4.2 Winning the reward. The reward given for a transitory contest, which is greater than those contests and persecutions.
4.3: 4.3 But the multiplying brood of the wicked. He speaks alternately of Catholics and heretics, to show the praiseworthy wisdom of the former and the blameworthy cunning of the latter. Plantings. Since in Greek [the word] is called calf in Latin, some did not understand that they were plantings, and interpreted them as vitulamina (shoots): this error has so taken possession of many codices that scarcely any is found written otherwise.
4.7: 4.7 The just man, etc. RAB. When he had spoken of the destruction of the wicked, etc., up to those from life to eternal death.
4.10: 4.10 Pleasing God. RAB. God does not take away, etc., up to hence Peter: God knoweth how to deliver the godly from temptation, but to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be tormented I Petr. 1..
4.12: 4.12 Fascination. THE SAME. By this sentence are noted, etc., up to for God has separated them from the company of the wicked, to hide them in the secret of his face from the disturbance of men Psal. 30..
4.19: 4.19 He will dash them puffed up and speechless, because they will be inexcusable: for when they knew God, they did not glorify him as God, or give thanks, but became vain in their thoughts Rom. 1..
5.1: 5.1 Then, etc. We are wearied, etc. RAB. The philosophers are wearied, etc., up to hence they say in sorrow, What hath pride profited us?
5.9: 5.9 Like a shadow. RAB. By the shadow is meant forgetfulness of mind, etc., up to which precede the end of corruptible life. THE SAME. By the bird is meant excellence, etc., up to groaning, they will be relieved by no voice of consolation.
5.14: 5.14 These things said in hell they who. He introduces four further kinds of images, by which he shows the foolish hope of the wicked, by which they think only of present measure, or that they will escape unpunished.
5.15: 5.15 Is the down which is carried away by the wind. Arising from the withered flower of grasses, it expresses the frailty of the flesh, which will quickly be carried away by the wind of sickness or by bodily distress, for all flesh is grass. And as a thin froth. Froth produced from waters floats on top of the water. This is the craving for human favor and for the boasting of the crowd, which is dissolved by the storm of temptation or by the examination of judgment, or is scattered, that is, it is proved how vain it was.
5.16: 5.16 But the just shall live for evermore. RAB. After the punishments of sinners, etc., up to they will enjoy God, in whom they have placed all their hope.
5.18: 5.18 He shall take armor. RAB. The Creator of all, etc., up to since they cannot resist him.
5.22: 5.22 And to a certain place. Wherever it is necessary: for that cannot be confused which is ordained by divine wisdom.
5.23: 5.23 And rivers, that is, the commotions of persecutions; for often the hearts of the wicked, which preaching does not soften, the scourge of gathering breaks.
6.1: 6.1 Better is wisdom, etc. RAB. He admonishes the rulers of the Church, etc., up to he will judge not only works, but thoughts and wills.
6.7: 6.7 For to him that is little, mercy is granted. That is, to those who have sinned through ignorance, or frailty, or necessity, and have blotted it out by humble penance. But the mighty shall be mightily, etc., namely those who, by despising the commandments of God, have committed grave sins and have not repented. For as they were more powerful in impiety, they will endure stronger torments of Gehenna. ANAST. For what cause, etc., up to but to whom much is given, of him much also shall be required.
6.8: 6.8 For he will not withdraw the person. Hence: God is not a respecter of persons, he judges every one according to his ways Act. 10..
6.10: 6.10 To you, therefore, O kings, etc. Having finished his speech to the powerful, and having rebuked their hardness with hard words, he turns his exhortation to the rulers of the Church, and extols wisdom with wondrous praises.
6.12: 6.12 Love, etc., and you shall have discipline. He who loves wisdom keeps discipline in his conduct. For he does not love wisdom who does not keep discipline. Hence: If you love me, keep my commandments Joan. 14..
6.14: 6.14 She preventeth them that covet her. Offering herself freely. For he himself is the way, the truth, and the life Joan. 14.: through him one goes, toward him one strives, to him one arrives.
6.15: 6.15 Sitting by him, etc. Always ready, namely, to help; hence: Behold, I stand at the door and knock; if any man shall open to me, I will come in to him and will sup with him, and he with me Apoc. 3.. In the present we must devote ourselves to wisdom, and live according to the rule of her discipline.
6.22: 6.22 If therefore you are delighted. RAB. He admonishes kings, etc., up to will attain the crown of the heavenly kingdom.
6.25: 6.25 Neither will I go with consuming envy. Envy has no share in wisdom, because through the envy of the devil death entered into the world, and through wisdom the human race is delivered from it.
6.27: 6.27 Therefore receive. RAB. Wisdom, about to show, etc., up to are said to be more perfect, healing, and life-giving.
7.5: 7.5 For no king. RAB. He shows that every man, etc., up to as Jesus Christ is perfect God, so he is also perfect man.
7.9: 7.9 Neither did I compare, etc. Hence: Having found one precious pearl, he sells all and buys it. For he who truly finds heavenly wisdom, that is the word of God, despises all the advantages of the present life, philosophy, eloquence, and strives to devote himself to divine contemplation.
7.11: 7.11 There came, etc. RAB. Solomon, having experienced this, etc., up to hence the sun also, because it alone shines by day among the stars, is so named.
7.15: 7.15 She herself is the guide of wisdom. RAB. God the Father of the incarnate Son, to whom he gave all power in heaven and on earth.
7.17: 7.17 For he himself. RAB. Of Solomon the Scripture says, God gave, etc., up to for he enlightens every man coming into this world, and he who follows him does not walk in darkness Joan. 1.
7.22: 7.22 For in her is the spirit of understanding, holy, etc. RAB. As Isaiah shows, all the gifts of the Holy Spirit exist in the humanity of the Savior, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge, and the fullness of the Godhead, to whom the Spirit is not given by measure. THE SAME. The Spirit who fills all things is called at once mobile and stable. For man runs about everywhere, meets one everywhere, and is suddenly found where he is not believed to be. The almighty Spirit, therefore, that he may be signified as present everywhere, is called at once stable and mobile. THE SAME. Hence: The brightness of his glory and the figure of his substance Heb. 1., upholding all things by the word, etc., up to in time the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us.
8.1: 8.1 She reacheth from end. That is, from the beginning of the world to the coming of Christ, she powerfully asserts the wonderful works and sincere testimonies through the Old Testament, and from the incarnation of the Word to the end of the world she sets forth the sweetness of the Gospel. From end to end, therefore, she reaches mightily, because everywhere she acts perfectly: for end signifies perfection.
8.3: 8.3 She glorifieth her fellowship, that is, she represents the nobility of him, namely the Father, who is coeternal and co-omnipotent with her; or it can be read partly of the temporal birth, partly of the eternal. She has the fellowship of God. That is, the humanity in which God dwells, who is the wisdom of the Father. Or she glorifies the nobility of him, that is, of God the Father; that is, she is of the same essence as the Father, begotten from eternity, born in time of a mother.
8.4: 8.4 For she is the teacher of discipline. Of his fullness we have all received: through him grace and truth was made, that is, revealed. No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him Joan. 1..
8.7: 8.7 And the labors of this. For there is nothing slothful in her works. Whatever things are true, whatever modest, whatever just, she does, and entrusts what is to be done to her own. For sobriety and wisdom. RAB. He who is temperate, etc., up to and gave her to Jacob his servant.
8.11: 8.11 Admirable. The childbearing of the Virgin was to be wondered at by all, because he was set for the resurrection and the fall of many, he who stands for a sign of the peoples, before whom kings shall shut their mouths, whom the nations shall beseech.
8.16: 8.16 Entering into my house. RAB. After preaching, after the labor of the work, in which the saints offer comfort to their hearers, returning to themselves they devote themselves to divine contemplation, where they find the rest of heavenly sweetness. THE SAME, from Greg. Bodily delights, etc., up to hence David: Taste and see that the Lord is sweet Psal. 33., etc. ORIG. He who opens the mute mouth, etc., up to but justice, because he is the distributor and judge of merits.
8.19: 8.19 And I was a witty child, etc. RAB. Solomon in his boyhood asked of God wisdom, that he might judge the people rightly and discern between good and evil: he was therefore made most wise, and he seems to have obtained a good soul, who had a wise and understanding heart. But how does what is said agree with him:
8.20: 8.20 I came to a body undefiled, etc., when he loved a foreign woman and built idols? It seems, then, to fit better the people of the saints, who, regenerated in baptism and imbued with faith in the Savior, received the boyhood of their good nature and simple innocence, and strove with every effort to reach the summit of virtues: hence it follows: And whereas I was more good, etc. The Father judgeth no man, but hath given all judgment to the Son. His members have become imitators of him.
9.7: 9.7 But thou hast chosen, etc. RAB. David, because a man, etc., up to the power and wisdom of God, and the image of the invisible God.
9.13: 9.13 For what man. He marvels at the excellence of God. As if to say: O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God! Rom. 11. And, Who hath known the mind of the Lord, or who hath been his counselor? Isa. 40.
9.17: 9.17 And thy mind. No one knows what is done in the heart of man but the spirit of man, and no one knows the things of God but the Spirit of God. And the Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God, he who enlightens the hearts of the saints.
10.1: 10.1 She preserved him that was first. RAB. The first man, created by the goodness of God, placed in paradise, set over all living creatures, was cast down by the transgression of the commandment into the miseries of this world; and his being restored by the wisdom of God, that is, Christ, is a great sign of divine piety.
10.3: 10.3 The unjust in his anger. As Cain, who unjustly slew his brother, the vengeance of whose crime was paid in the flood, and the generation of Cain was destroyed: but the wisdom of God preserved Noe, of the line of Seth, with his sons in the ark for the restoration of the world.
10.5: 10.5 She also in the consent of pride, etc. RAB. The devil through pride, etc., up to the humility of Christ united.
10.6: 10.6 She the just, etc. Hence Peter says: Reducing the cities of the Sodomites and Gomorrhites into ashes, he condemned them with an overthrow, making them an example to those that after should do wickedly; and delivered the just Lot, oppressed by the injuries of the wicked and their lewd conversation II Petr. 2., etc. Lot's wife, looking back, was turned into a pillar of salt, lest we who by the grace of God have been called to life should look back upon the old man, remaining in the midst of the way. Turned into a pillar of salt she seasons others, hence: Remember Lot's wife Luc. 17., that is, that we may not be negligent like fools, but may take prudent care.
10.8: 10.8 For wisdom, etc. And these things, etc. Jacob, fleeing Esau his brother, came to Laban his uncle, and on the way saw in a dream a ladder set up, and the angels of God ascending and descending, and the Lord himself leaning upon the ladder, saying to him: I am the God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac; the land whereon thou sleepest I will give to thee and to thy seed Gen. 28.. And coming into Mesopotamia he took Lia and Rachel, for whom he long fed the sheep of Laban. Who wished to cheat him of his wages. But by the wisdom of God Laban was deprived and Jacob enriched, and he returned with many riches. Mystically, however, these things pertain to the martyrs, whom the mercy of Christ delivered from their persecutors, strengthening them with the grace of the Holy Spirit and the hope of future reward; and at length, their enemies being conquered, he brought them to the kingdom of heaven, to the praise and glory of his name.
10.13: 10.13 She sold just man, etc. RAB. Mystically, the Wisdom of God rescued the martyrs from persecutions and exalted them in the heavenly kingdom. Hence they are to come with Christ as judges of their enemies.
10.15: 10.15 She delivered the just people. RAB. Mystically. God delivers his elect from their persecutors, etc., up to to the rewards of the kingdom, where they sing praises without end to their deliverer.
10.21: 10.21 For wisdom, etc. Without the wisdom of God neither can the human mind think anything worthily, nor the mouth utter it: from him, therefore, both wisdom and eloquence must be sought.
11.1: 11.1 He said the works, etc. RAB. The Christian people follow prophecy through the desert of this world, that they may come to the homeland of the heavenly kingdom; hence Peter: We have the more firm prophetical word, whereunto you do well to attend, as to a light that shineth in a dark place II Petr. 1., etc.
11.4: 11.4 Out of the high rock, etc. But the rock was Christ, who, struck by the rod of the cross, which was in the hands, that is, in the writings of the prophets, poured forth living water.
11.5: 11.5 For by what things, etc. RAB. Having recalled the benefits, etc., up to whether therefore they suffer or not, there is glory for them.
11.10: 11.10 For when they were tried. RAB. God chastised the sinning Israelites with fitting plagues, and comforted them when repentant; the Egyptians and Chanaanites he destroyed as unworthy of mercy. Torments, etc. By Pharao, wherever they might be, that is. Or, not only those whom the Israelites slew by recent slaughter in each city were punished, but all the Chanaanites hearing of the victory of the people of God; hence Rahab says: The dread of you is fallen upon us Jos. 2., etc. Mystically, however, the Jews, who despised the incarnation of the Son of God and his preaching, wander everywhere over the earth, and as fugitives are afflicted with various disasters. But the Gentiles, converted to the faith and receiving paternal correction, do not depart from the mercy of God: so that those who had been at the head are at the tail, and the reverse.
11.13: 11.13 Double, etc. The remembrance of past evils is not lessened, and the storm of present ones is increased. Hence they have no hope of remedy, because, feigning repentance, they do not strive for amendment; hence: When he slew them, then they sought him, and they loved him Psal. 77., etc.
11.15: 11.15 Not in like manner to the just, etc. Because they do not sin alike. For the just man falls seven times and rises again; but the wicked man, when he is come into the depth of evils, contemns.
11.16: 11.16 Because certain erring, etc. RAB. It was fitting, etc., up to for their whole intention is to persecute the human race and torment it in every way.
11.21: 11.21 But all things in measure, etc. RAB. Because all things according to truth, etc., up to when the hidden things of darkness shall be enlightened and the counsels of hearts shall be made manifest.
11.23: 11.23 The turning of the scale, etc. Isaiah says something similar: Behold the Gentiles are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the smallest grain of a balance Isa. 40.; for he wants it to be understood that the mind, and reason, and sense of the Lord, through whom all things were made, and without whom nothing was made, is he of whom it is said: By the word of the Lord the heavens were established Psal. 32., etc. All the nations that have not known their Creator are, in comparison with God, as a drop of a bucket, and as the turning of the scale, which is easily tipped, and as a drop of the morning dew Sap. 11., which at the first look of the sun is dried up. Or as a drop from a bucket, if it flows from the one carrying it, is despised or neglected: so the multitude of the nations, compared with the heavenly splendor, the supernal mysteries, and the multitude of angels, is counted as nothing.
11.25: 11.25 For thou lovest, etc. A good craftsman both loves and rules his own work; and if man sometimes sins, he bears with him in great patience, and through penance converts him to the better. Hence: He maketh his sun to rise upon the good and the bad, and raineth upon the just and the unjust Matth. 5.; but the impenitent are condemned by just judgment: For the Lord is just, and hath loved justice Psal. 10..
12.1: 12.1 O how good and sweet, etc. Through those whom thou fillest, or through others whom thou wilt; hence: He will convince the world of sin, and of justice, and of judgment Joan. 16..
12.3: 12.3 For those old inhabitants. RAB. He speaks historically, etc., up to with the help of the Holy Spirit, will bring forth useful fruits.
12.12: 12.12 For who shall say, etc. RAB. He shows by manifest reason that the Creator is not to be contradicted if he disposes his creature according to his own will: because all things are placed in his will, and there is none who can resist him. He is just in all his ways Psal. 144.; hence it follows, Whereas thou art just Rom. 9., etc.
12.15: 12.15 Whereas therefore, etc. Hence: Many are the scourges of the sinner, but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord Psal. 31.. There is a great distance between the judgment of the elect and of the reprobate. The former the Lord corrects that he may amend them; the latter pay the penalties of pride and faithlessness, that they may know they cannot fight against the Ruler of all. Happy the judge who always looks to the piety and goodness of his own judge. For judgment without mercy to him that hath not done mercy. Jac. 2..
12.16: 12.16 For thy power, etc. Because the judgment of God, whether in the correction of the elect or in the damnation of the wicked, is the perfection of supreme equity: and therefore by his goodness he long defers and suspends judgment, that he may have more to whom to give his benefit. For when the creature lifts itself up against the Creator it is justly punished with vengeance, that it may know itself to be inferior. These words can be referred to the passion of Christ, whom the Father delivered to death for us, and made him sin for us who knew not sin: who, unless he had undergone an undeserved death, would not have delivered us from the death we deserved. The Father, therefore, being just, punishing the just one, justly disposes all things. Almighty God judges all things with the greatest tranquillity: yet human feelings and members are ascribed to him by a figure of speech, so that divine utterances may be adapted to our capacity. For we read in the Scriptures of the eyes of the Lord, ears, hands, mouth, feet, anger, fury, and the like, though a simple nature never admits variety, nor true unity division. But one and the same works many and diverse things: Hence: Thou shalt change them, and they shall be changed; but thou art the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail Psal. 101., etc. And elsewhere: I am God, and I change not Mal. 3.. And elsewhere: With whom there is no change Jac. 1., etc. And thou hast taught thy people: by the wonderful works of God the faithful are instructed, so that they may not be entangled with the wicked, but may strive to keep themselves uncontaminated by confessing and hoping in the Lord, and not neglect the time of penance.
12.23: 12.23 Senseless, etc., so that those who would not acknowledge and honor the Creator were fittingly handed over to a reprobate sense, to do things that are not fitting, dishonoring their bodies in themselves: Because they changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature rather than the Creator Rom. 1..
12.26: 12.26 But they that were not amended by mockeries, etc. That is, those who, scourged by God, were not corrected, experienced fitting damnation: God corrects to this end, that he may amend. But he who, ungrateful and impatient, murmurs, is led from temporal torment to eternal.
12.27: 12.27 For in these things, etc. RAB. The Gentile world, while it served idols, etc., up to inflicts eternal punishment on the uncorrected.
13.1: 13.1 Knowledge. That is, fear and reverence. Hence: Behold the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to depart from evil is understanding. For he departs from evil who departs from the worship of idols: he fears God who keeps his commandments: for The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. A good understanding to all that do it Psal. 110.. From these works, namely of man, they could have known the good craftsman, who properly is, because immutable and always the same, always remaining in himself, he rules all things. The vainest vanity, therefore, of men, who venerate creatures instead of the Creator. Nor by the works. Some worshipped fire, which they called Vulcan; others the ether or air, which they called Jupiter and Juno; others abundant water, that is Neptune; others the circuit of the stars, who distributed the positions and course of the stars among various shapes of animals; others the sun, which they called Phoebus; others the moon, that is, Diana. RAB. They sin in two ways, etc., up to in which the covetousness of man is condemned.
13.6: 13.6 But yet, etc. Hence Paul says: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all impiety of those men that detain the truth of God in injustice; because that which is known of God is manifest in them Rom. 1., etc. The knowledge of God is gained from the fabric of the world. For that the invisible God might be known from invisible things, a work was made by him which would manifest the maker, so that he might be understood to be the God of all, who made what others cannot. But when they knew, they did not glorify him as God, but became vain in their thoughts RAB.
13.10: 13.10 Unhappy, etc. Namely, those who honor gods in order to feast their eyes on gold, and on the gleam of polished marble or ivory, or garments distinguished by gems and colors: and the more adorned the temples and the more beautiful the images, the more majesty they have, or are said to have. It is religion, therefore, or is believed to be, what human covetousness admires.
13.11: 13.11 Or if some artificer. RAB. Wisdom mocks those, etc., up to Whose god is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame Philip. 3..
14.1: 14.1 Again another, to sail, etc. These things also are said against idolatry. For it is the greatest folly that a man, made to the image of God, having from him a rational mind with which he has devised how to cross the waves, building a ship according to the skill of his art, should not honor him who gave him this knowledge, and should invoke an idol, which he formed with like art and greater vanity. For since he who makes is greater than what is made, to adore one's own handiwork is madness. The course of sailing is to be asked of God, from whom comes the preparation of the vessel. Heretics, however, who fashion vain images of errors, perish in the waves of the world for this reason, that they have left the ship of the Church, and God the helmsman.
14.3: 14.3 Because thou hast given. By the power of God he led the Israelites through the Red Sea with dry foot, and divided the waters of the Jordan, to strike terror into the nations that were to be exterminated; and for the faithful also, amid the waves and persecutions of the world, he prepares a path of faith and constancy, that they may pass over unharmed, and there is no need of human comfort where God shows the wonderful effects of his power.
14.5: 14.5 But that the works, etc. The Creator gave knowledge to his creature, by which it might take counsel for itself in the present, so as to serve his will. Hence he commanded Noe to make an ark, in which he and his offspring would be saved, and the other living creatures would be kept for the restoration of the world, when the human race was destroyed by the flood for its iniquity; hence Peter: Wherein a few, that is, eight souls, were saved by water: whereunto baptism being of the like form, now saveth you also Petr. 3., etc. The ark, built of smoothed wood, signifies the Church, which is made from the gathering of the faithful by the skill of the preachers. A few, that is, eight souls were saved by water, the world perishing: because in comparison with the reprobate the number of the elect is small. For few there are that find the way of life. The water of the flood killed those placed outside, because the very waters which lifted the ark to heaven plunge the heretic, though he has the sacrament of baptism, down to hell. The number eight also signifies the Church, because it receives the washing of baptism in the sacrament of the Lord's resurrection. That as he rose from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we also may walk in newness of life, washed by the water of regeneration. Hence Jeremias: Every man is become a fool by his knowledge, the founder is confounded in his graven work: for the thing he hath cast is a lie, and there is no breath in them. They are vain works, and worthy to be laughed at, and in the time of their visitation they shall perish Jerem. 10..
14.8: 14.8 And he that made it. The image and the worship of false gods. For the devil will be punished for this, that he usurps divine honor for himself; and man, who honors the creature instead of the Creator. Wood, however, often signifies man. Blessed, therefore, is the man who speaks and does the truth. But the heretic, who worships his own fabrications, is accursed and given over to perdition, and so is his work, that is, his doctrine.
14.11: 14.11 Therefore for this. Idols are not to be spared, nor their inhabitants, that is, the demons, because they draw men made in the image of God away from him, and overthrow them in the snare of error. Heretics also, who seduce men, will not escape strict judgment.
14.12: 14.12 The beginning. For it is the worst kind of fornication, by which the soul departs from God and fornicates with idols, or leaves the truth of divine doctrine and follows the falsehood of heretical perversity or opinion. Hence Paul calls avarice the service of idols. Whence it is clear that all evil concupiscence is called fornication, by which the soul, having left the higher law for the pleasure of lower things, is corrupted, cast down or prostituted, as if for the base wage of natures.
14.13: 14.13 For neither, etc. May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips, and all who speak a lie Psal. 11.. Hence Jeremias: The gods that have not made heaven and earth, let them perish from the earth Jer. 11., etc.; LACT. vol. 1. On account of the folly of men, etc., up to they paid divine honors to their parents, and ordered them to be paid.
14.21: 14.21 The incommunicable name. The incommunicable name, namely, of Almighty God; who alone is incomprehensible; they ascribed it to insensible and fragile matter or an image.
14.23: 14.23 For either they sacrificed their own children. As in the rites of Saturn, to whom, out of hatred of Jupiter, they immolated their little ones without regard for piety, and the priests of Bellona sacrificed with their own blood. Hence Quintilian: If, he says, a god compels this, he is angry: and if he is angry, he does not accept your sacrifices. Or used hidden sacrifices. As they did in the rites of Egyptian Isis and Eleusinian Ceres. For as there Osiris is sought with the lamentation of his mother, so here Proserpina, carried off for the incestuous marriage of her uncle Pluto. Because Ceres is said to have sought her in Sicily with torches lit from Etna, her rites were celebrated with the brandishing of burning torches. Similarly in the rites of Father Liber they rave, and of the Great Mother, where, after the example of the gods who, sated at the festival, spent the whole night in revelry, they play. Because they thought to please their gods through lust and uncleanness.
14.25: 14.25 All things mingled. For all things were confused: there was no reason there, no true religion. The more wicked one was, the more he thought he pleased his god.
14.27: 14.27 For the worship of abominable. There is no greater madness than to forsake the living God and serve the dead. For when the mind turns away from its Creator, it is entangled in all crimes. For the beginning of all sin is pride Eccli. 10.. The end. The consummation and fullness. For those who worship an idol in place of God, all things in them are reckoned as sin.
14.28: 14.28 For either while they are merry. Because when they swear, they pollute the name of God, who says: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain, and swear not by the name of foreign gods Exod. 20.; but while they think they mock God, they cast themselves headlong into eternal death. Heretics, however, worshipping the images of their errors, become the cause of their own perdition; their doctrine is false, their life unjust, their joy insane, their death abominable: because when they swear unjustly by an idol, and do not hope in their God, therefore they will receive vengeance for their deserts. Hence it follows: For it is not the power of them that swear.
15.1: 15.1 But thou, etc. RAB. For those condemned by just judgment, repenting too late, acknowledge what they previously would not believe; hence: The Lord shall be known when he executeth judgments, the sinner hath been caught in the works of his own hands Psal. 9.; hence John: Every one that hath this hope in him sanctifieth himself, as he also is holy: and whosoever abideth in him sinneth not I Joan. 3..
15.3: 15.3 For to know thee, etc. It is the perception of incorruption, and in the future of contemplation; hence: This is eternal life, that they may know thee, the only true God Joan. 17., etc.
15.4: 15.4 For neither hath the mischievous. He speaks in the person of the faithful, who, fortified by the grace of God, have not mingled themselves with the iniquity or idolatry of the Gentiles: because this labor is without fruit of justice, and deserves eternal death.
15.6: 15.6 Lovers of evil things, etc. Let them become like to them that make them, and all such as trust in them Psal. 134.. The inventors also of false doctrines and their worshippers are worthy of death. For God will destroy the man who has done these things, that is, the master and his disciple. Above he rejected idols of wood, stone, or bronze; now he condemns also those of clay. For it was justly rendered to them that, as they were made of earth, because they would not follow the better part of themselves, that is, the soul created in the image of God to acknowledge the living God, they should, by imitating the viler part of themselves, the earthly body, adore a god of mud, and without the fruit of good work be rendered useless to insensible earth, from which, being insensible, they were taken. Mystically, however, heretics and schismatics, who detain the truth of God in injustice, and worship a lie in place of truth in the images of their doctrine, though they cloak it with eloquence or feigned virtue, yet what they fashion is fragile and made of clay.
15.10: 15.10 Their heart is ashes, and their thought foul, and their life baser than mud; because they know not their maker, and vanish away in their thoughts. They despise the sense of the holy fathers, and for human favor and earthly gain fashion new errors like vain games; erring, namely, and sending others into error, so that they may be inexcusable: when God shall judge the secrets of hearts, and shall render to every one according to his works.
15.13: 15.13 For this man knoweth, etc. Heretics have no excuse; because they sin knowingly, when they refuse to imitate sound faith and right doctrine, following an earthly and fragile sense rather than a spiritual one.
15.17: 15.17 Better is. Because man is better than idols according to the reason of creation; because he lives and understands, whereas they never do. But because he follows the vanity of error more than the knowledge of truth, when he is in honor he does not understand: and he is compared to senseless beasts Psal. 48..
15.18: 15.18 Senseless. As if to say: they had no discernment. For in truth living things are better than dead, sensible than insensible, rational than irrational. But it was fitting that those who were ignorant of the Creator should not know distinction among creatures. For he who neglects to have in himself the praise and blessing of God shows himself erring in the discernment of animals.
16.2: 16.2 For which things, etc. RAB. The people of Israel in the desert craved flesh, etc., up to and therefore they were justly handed over to be tormented.
16.6: 16.6 But not for ever. RAB. For the brazen serpent, etc., up to because he died through his humanity, he is as it were of bronze through his Divinity.
16.9: 16.9 For them, etc. The elect are proved by affliction, and are warned to avoid sins and do good. The reprobate are scattered, because they are not corrected. Therefore small animals kill the idolaters. But serpents cannot destroy the Israelites, worshippers of God; because the Lord knows how to deliver the godly from temptation, but to reserve the unjust for the day of judgment to be tormented.
16.12: 16.12 But thy word, O Lord. That is, the Son, through whom are all things, whose power is everywhere, who has done all things whatsoever he willed; he himself heals bodies, he himself saves souls from spiritual beasts.
16.14: 16.14 But man killeth. CHRYS. Man through malice, etc., up to is free from every crime.
16.16: 16.16 For denying to know thee, etc. RAB. The Egyptians were afflicted with diverse plagues, etc., up to because all things consent to the will of the Creator.
16.18: 16.18 For at one time. RAB. As we read in Genesis: The Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrha brimstone and fire, to destroy the wicked: and in Exodus, hail and fire together. In the book of Numbers: He sent fiery serpents against those who murmured, that the wicked may know that every creature is ready to avenge the injury done to the Creator.
16.20: 16.20 Instead of which things, etc. RAB. In the desert manna was given to the children of Israel, etc., up to Many are the scourges of the sinner, but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord Psal. 31..
16.24: 16.24 For the creature, etc. RAB. Let sinners be confounded here: who, though the other creatures serve their maker, resist him. Hence they are scourged by the concord of all creatures: and if they do not repent, they will be tormented for ever; but for the good, true goods are prepared.
16.25: 16.25 Therefore, etc. RAB. God rained manna from heaven, etc., up to like a transgressor of the law he will perish for ever.
16.28: 16.28 That it might be known to all, etc. RAB. This food literally nourished, etc., up to but at the rising of the sun, that is, of Christ, let us say: The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us.
17.1: 17.1 For great. RAB. Mystically. All the persecutors of the Church of Christ suffer the darkness of their crimes, and can never be secure, being vexed by the rulers of these darkenesses, even to the exterior darkness, where there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth; hence: Every one that doth evil hateth the light Joan. 3., etc. Hence Paul: You were sometime darkness, but now light in the Lord Ephes. 5., etc.
17.4: 17.4 Neither. For horror always accompanies darkness: and the less one discerns what is around him, the more he fears, trembling at adversities on every side. So the Egyptians for three days suffered the greatest darkness, which neither sun nor stars could illumine, and wherever they lay they trembled with excessive terror; and when he says that sad persons frightened them, it could be that demons put forward certain phantasms to terrify them, to increase their punishments. The persecutors also of the faith and of the truth are surrounded by the darkness of sins, because they know not the sun of justice, and the preachers do not enlighten them with the splendor of doctrine. A sound also coming down, that is, heavenly threatening, disturbs them, and sad persons, that is, demons, who will at some time torture them, terrify them; and yet they do not do penance fruitfully: but, despairing, they treasure up to themselves wrath against the day of judgment.
17.6: 17.6 Full of fear. Because they dreaded punishments on every side. For the graver the pains, the greater the horrors that are feared. And of the magic art, etc. RAB. When the Magi in Egypt, etc., up to and the ancient serpent with his angels, a savage enemy, patiently.
17.9: 17.9 And the air, etc. RAB. He notes the excess of fear which they suffer, their conscience reproving them with the punishments that threaten; for wickedness, always timid, gives the sign of its own dread, and is condemned by punishment.
17.11: 17.11 Betrayal, etc. Namely, fear betrays the weakness of the proud man, who exalts himself with a vain hope of helps, thinking that he can do what he cannot or could not do: and while his strength is less, he thinks the power of the things he suffers from outside to be greater. This frequently happens to persecutors of the faithful, who think themselves powerful when they torture the saints, but, conquered by their power and saddened by anguish of mind, they recognize that they cannot do what they desired and that the strength of God, who thus conquers in his soldiers, is greater.
17.13: 17.13 But they, etc. RAB. The Egyptians, namely, surrounded by the horror of darkness, etc., up to they dreaded as dangerous.
17.19: 17.19 For the whole world. As if to say: the wicked were in darkness, but wherever the children of Israel dwelt, there was light.
17.20: 17.20 The image of darkness. Spiritual darkness is graver than bodily: because it leads men to the exterior darkness, where there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, which the Egyptian darkness prefigures. For as there bodies are useful for no good work, so here souls together with bodies are condemned to an eternal prison; where there is neither reason, nor place, nor time of working.
18.1: 18.1 But to thy saints. RAB. The Israelites in Egypt, etc., up to protects in prosperity and in adversity.
18.4: 18.4 Worthy indeed, etc. RAB. The Egyptians deservedly suffered the punishment of darkness, etc., up to the reason of which mystery was prefigured in the ancient fathers, and fulfilled in the coming of Christ.
18.9: 18.9 For secretly did they sacrifice. RAB. The people of Israel in Egypt celebrated the Pasch at the command of the Lord, etc., up to but in the hidden place of the heart they always sacrifice to the Lord, hence: A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit Psal. 50.. And elsewhere: In me, O God, are thy vows Psal. 55., etc. THE SAME. He recalls that God struck the firstborn of Egypt, where the Egyptians no longer pretended as before, but openly compelled the people of God to depart, saying: We shall all die Exod. 11..
18.15: 18.15 Thy almighty word. The Son, of whom it is said: In the beginning was the Word Joan. 1., etc., is here named arm and right hand: on account of the effective power of divine might. He then, through the ministry of an angel, executed his judgments on the firstborn of the Egyptians, he who afterwards sanctified to himself the firstborn of the Hebrews. Now also through the water of baptism he saves the multitude of believers, and slays the multitude of spiritual enemies.
18.19: 18.19 Visions. RAB. This belongs to divine goodness, which chastises sinners that they may abstain and do penance. But if they abuse the patience of God, they will be punished for ever without excuse.
18.20: 18.20 And the just also were then touched. RAB. He recalls, etc., up to through whom we can escape destruction.
18.24: 18.24 For in the garment of the high priest. RAB. The Hebrews assign byssus to the earth, etc., up to in the pontifical figure, he foreknew that Christ would come, but because he had seen him clothed in flesh, he believed him not God but a mere man; hence: If they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory I Cor. 2..
19.1: 19.1 But the wicked, etc. The enemies of the people of God: vengeance came upon them to the utmost, because they corrected neither their life nor their morals, for by feigned arguments they pretended repentance, and therefore did not deserve indulgence. Hence Pharao, when afflicted with plagues, promised that he would let the people of God go, but, breathing again a little, returned to his domestic cruelty, until he was drowned by the waves in the Red Sea. So the persecutors of the Christian name, if they persist in their malice, will feel in punishment how much the justice of God avails.
19.8: 19.8 Seeing thy wonders. So we ought, rejoicing, to give thanks to our deliverer, saying: Bless the Lord, O my soul Psal. 103.. Hence the Apostle: Pray without ceasing, in all things give thanks I Thess. 5..
19.10: 19.10 The earth brought forth. Note that for the enemies of God the earth brought forth flies, and the river frogs; but to the worshippers of God the earth gave fruit, and the sea food of flesh. For it is fitting that divine providence should provide nourishment for his faithful through his works, and should bring fitting torment upon his enemies through the creature subject to him. For they justly suffered. RAB. He who the ancient servants of God, etc., up to does not know the way of truth, and does not find the door which is Christ.
19.17: 19.17 In themselves the elements. As in an organ different sounds agree by tempering into the concord of a melody, so discordant elements, the right of nature being preserved, are bent to the will of the Creator: for he did not make a creature contrary to himself, but in all things consonant with his will. Hence to be judged, etc. RAB. For men and beasts, etc., up to so that it might appear that the elements of the world serve not only their own condition but the will of the Creator.
19.20: 19.20 For in all things thou hast magnified. The Lord, merciful and compassionate, is always present with his faithful, whom he always protects and rules: whom he at times purges in martyrdom. Hence: The furnace trieth the potter's vessels, and the temptation of tribulation just men Eccl. 27.. For many are the afflictions of the just, and out of them all the Lord delivereth them.
